title: log3gpp: Build the packet record at the end of parse_line.
description:
**I think I'll end my gratuitous refactoring of the log3gpp parser with this commit.**  There was an earlier question about the intended lifetime of `protocol.parameters`; Its current persistence across records seems like it might have been unintentional, but making a safe decision about that will depend on someone having more understanding of the _intent_ of the file structure than I have... or someone more willing to boldly modify the current behavior than I am. :grin:

----

Function parse_line currently collects a bunch of information about the parsed
line, and, upon success, callsites use the collected information to build a
packet in 'rec'.  Rather than have both callsites manage all those variables
and arguments, let's roll it into parse_line, eliminating another round of
duplicated code and declarations.

In theory, build_packet_record could be expanded directly into
parse_line_into_record, but that might become unwieldy.

notes.body:
> I think I'll end my gratuitous refactoring of the log3gpp parser with this commit.

If it reduces duplication of code - or almost-duplication with some of the differences being at least gratuitous (in the first sense) and possibly buggy - that's definitely not gratuitous in the "uncalled for; lacking good reason; unwarranted" sense, although, as we, at least, haven't paid you for your work improving the code, it may be gratuitous in the "given or done free of charge" sense. :-)

> In theory, build_packet_record could be expanded directly into parse_line_into_record, but that might become unwieldy.

In practice, the compiler might do it for you (and you can give it further encouragement by declaring `build_packet_record` to be `static inline`). [Inlining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inline_expansion) rules, especially if either 1) the inlined function is only being called from one location in the code or 2) the inlined code isn't much bigger than (or is the same size or ''smaller'' than after other optimizations are done) the call that was eliminated.
